And now I bet on sixteen red!
Red came up again, you won again!
You see, today is simply my lucky day!

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
We will take her in it.
The driver was taking passengers to the station.

examples.text: Отлично. На ней её и везём.
examples.trans: Excellent. We will take her in it.

meanings.note: 'взять на работу' = to give someone a job
'взять на работу' = to give someone a job

examples.text: Вот и возьмите на работу Галилея.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.
My grandmother turned eighty years old.

examples.text: Вы когда взяли книгу Носова? В восемьдесят четвёртом году!
examples.trans: When did you borrow Nosov's book? In the year eighty-four!
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'играть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to win', paired with 'выигрывать'.

examples.text: Паша, эти выборы ты не выиграешь.
examples.trans: Pasha, you won't win this election.

meanings.note: money won in gambling or lottery

examples.text: Вот это да, забери свой большой выигрыш!
examples.trans: Wow look at that, take your big winnings!

examples.text: Пожалуйста, вот ваш выигрыш, забирайте фишки.
examples.trans: Please, here is your winnings, take the chips.

examples.text: Я не выходил! Я выпал из окна!
examples.trans: I didn't walk out! I fell out the window!
The first snow fell during the night.

examples.text: Ещё раз вам говорю, я не выходил! Я выпал из окна!
examples.trans: I'm telling you again, I didn't walk out! I fell out the window!

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.note: Я тебе говорю = I'm telling you
emphatic at the start of a sentence
'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.
That is better than twelve years.

examples.text: Это гораздо лучше, чем двенадцать лет. Согласитесь?
examples.trans: That's much better than twelve years. Don't you agree?

examples.text: А тебе этого мало? У меня пенсия двенадцать тысяч!
examples.trans: And is that a small sum to you? My pension is twelve thousand!

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: забирать деньги = to take the money
забирать детей из школы = to pick the kids up from school

examples.trans: I pick the children up from school.

examples.text: А я тебе делаю условный срок. Плюс ты забираешь все деньги Вики.
examples.trans: And I get you a suspended sentence. Plus you take all of Vika's money.

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement
забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.
Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
The children are playing in the courtyard.

examples.text: Хорошая фотография! Напиши: трус не играет в хоккей.
examples.trans: Good photo! Write: a coward doesn't play hockey.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.
And that is Osipenko's cousin's company!
He works at a large company.

examples.text: Не все компании такие добрые, как наша.
examples.trans: Not all companies are as kind as ours.
And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: used as noun: на красное = on red (in roulette)

examples.text: Я ставлю все фишки на красное!
examples.trans: I bet all the chips on red!

examples.text: Я ставлю все фишки на двенадцать красное!
examples.trans: I put all the chips on twelve red!

examples.text: А теперь я ставлю на шестнадцать красное!
examples.trans: And now I bet on sixteen red!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: monster, beast (admiring slang for exceptional skill)

examples.trans: Well you are a real beast, Samson!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

examples.text: Говорят, что всем новичкам всегда везёт.
examples.trans: They say that all beginners always get lucky.

examples.text: Ты шутишь, шеф никогда не берёт новичков!
examples.trans: You are joking, the chef never takes novices!

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.
I'll definitely buy you a tank.

examples.text: Государство обязательно увидит и назначит операцию.
examples.trans: The state will surely see and will schedule the surgery.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('huge, enormous').

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

поднять.gloss: to lift, to raise; to rouse

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.

Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.note: the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'обственный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('own, proper').

examples.text: Я хочу купить собственную строительную компанию.
examples.trans: I want to buy my own construction company.

meanings.en: to put, to place in an upright position

examples.trans: Where should I put the plate?
Put the kettle on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'такан'). Common masculine noun meaning 'glass, tumbler' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Принесите нам ещё два стакана коньяка, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Bring us two more glasses of cognac, please!

examples.text: Сколько именно виски нужно наливать в стаканы?
examples.trans: How much whiskey exactly do I need to pour into the glasses?

meanings.note: relating to construction work or materials

examples.text: Это договор на покупку строительного оборудования.
examples.trans: This is a contract for the purchase of construction equipment.
He works at a construction company.

examples.text: Я хочу купить собственную строительную компанию.
examples.trans: I want to buy my own construction company.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'умма'). Common feminine noun meaning 'sum, amount' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
The film has a happy ending.

examples.text: Ты сейчас один против всех. Счастливого конца не будет.
examples.trans: Right now you're alone against everyone. There won't be a happy ending.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

examples.text: Я ставлю все фишки на красное.
examples.trans: I bet all the chips on red.

examples.text: Я ставлю все фишки на двенадцать красное!
examples.trans: I put all the chips on twelve red!

examples.text: Пожалуйста, вот ваш выигрыш, забирайте фишки.
examples.trans: Please, here is your winnings, take the chips.

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Core Russian num meaning 'sixteen' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А теперь я ставлю на шестнадцать красное!
examples.trans: And now I bet on sixteen red!

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
